name: Recurrence
description: A rule that turns into dated occurrences on the row (D152): calendar, an RFC 5545 RRULE from a wall start in a time zone; afterDone, an interval after the last completed occurrence; relative, an offset from a date field of the row a relation names, and its anniversaries. A due date on a weekend day or a holiday, a row of the holiday table the config names in the calendar a field of the row names, moves before or after it. The occurrences sub-table holds each occurrence up to horizonDays ahead: its due and open times, its state (upcoming, open, done, missed, skipped), and what and who completed it. An occurrence opens opensBefore its due, or, with none, when the one before it falls due; it reminds remindBefore its due and is missed overdueAfter it, each a deadline the API's behavior worker fires. A rule change regenerates the occurrences that have not opened and leaves the open ones as they are, and a missed occurrence never blocks the next. The behaviors' core alone implements it, on a table; no engine type composes it.

anchors.description: The anchors a row's recurrence may take: calendar, an RRULE from a start; afterDone, an interval after the last completion; relative, an offset from the date relative names.

timeZone.description: The IANA time zone a recurrence is read in when setRecurrence names none; UTC when absent.

horizonDays.description: How many days ahead the occurrences are kept materialised; 400 when absent.

historyDays.description: How many days a finished occurrence (done, missed, skipped) is kept after its due before a write prunes it; 1100 when absent.

adjust.description: How a due date on a weekend day or a holiday moves when setRecurrence names none: before, after, or none (it stays); none when absent.

weekendDays.description: The days a due date moves off, by English name; saturday and sunday when absent.

holidays.description: The holiday table: a table of the app's rows, each a date of a holiday calendar, and the field of this table that names a row's calendar.

calendarField.description: The holiday table's field that names its calendar.

dateField.description: The holiday table's date field: a Temporal.Date, or a string of a wall date.

field.description: This table's field that names the calendar a row's due dates move off; a row with none moves off weekend days alone.

relative.description: Where the relative anchor's date is: a to-one relation of this table and a date or date-time field of the table it points at.

type.description: The type the relation points at.

field.description: That type's date or date-time field.

opensBefore.description: How long before its due an occurrence opens, an ISO 8601 duration (P14D); with none it opens when the occurrence before it falls due, the first when it is planned.

remindBefore.description: How long before its due an occurrence reminds, an ISO 8601 duration (P3D): the deadline remind.

overdueAfter.description: How long after its due an open occurrence is missed, an ISO 8601 duration (P1D); at its due when absent.

permission.description: The permission complete and listOccurrences need; any caller when absent.

managePermission.description: The permission setRecurrence, skip and moveOne need; permission when absent.

fields.name: recurrence
fields.description: The row's recurrence as setRecurrence set it: its anchor, its rule and start, its every and offset, its time zone and adjustment, when it was set and its revision; absent until it is set.

fields.name: nextDueAt
fields.description: When the row's earliest occurrence that is upcoming or open falls due, in epoch milliseconds; absent when it has none.

fields.name: lastDoneAt
fields.description: When the row's latest occurrence was completed, in epoch milliseconds; absent before the first.

tables.name: occurrences
tables.description: One row per occurrence of the row's recurrence, keyed by its nominal wall date-time before any adjustment: its due and open times, its reminder and overdue times, its state, the revision of the recurrence that planned it, and what and who completed it. Upcoming ones up to horizonDays ahead; finished ones until historyDays after their due.

fields.name: key
fields.description: Its nominal wall date-time, before the adjustment (2026-10-31T09:00): its key on the row.

fields.name: due
fields.description: The wall date-time it falls due at, after the adjustment, in the recurrence's zone.

fields.name: dueAt
fields.description: When it falls due, in epoch milliseconds.

fields.name: opensAt
fields.description: When it opens, in epoch milliseconds.

fields.name: remindAt
fields.description: When it reminds, in epoch milliseconds; absent without remindBefore.

fields.name: overdueAt
fields.description: When it is missed unless done, in epoch milliseconds.

fields.name: state
fields.description: upcoming, open, done, missed or skipped.

fields.name: revision
fields.description: The revision of the row's recurrence that planned it or moved it last.

fields.name: shifted
fields.description: Why its due moved off its nominal date: weekend or holiday; absent when it did not.

fields.name: moved
fields.description: True once moveOne moved it.

fields.name: changedAt
fields.description: When its state last changed, in epoch milliseconds.

fields.name: remindedAt
fields.description: When its remind deadline fired, in epoch milliseconds; absent before.

fields.name: completedAt
fields.description: When it was completed, in epoch milliseconds; absent unless done.

fields.name: completedByTable
fields.description: The table of the row that completed it (a payment, a proof document), as references name a target; absent when none was named.

fields.name: completedByKey
fields.description: That row's key, as text.

fields.name: completedByPrincipal
fields.description: The subject of the principal that completed or skipped it.

fields.name: note
fields.description: What complete or skip said of it.

operations.name: setRecurrence
operations.description: Sets the row's recurrence: an anchor the config's anchors take, with its rule and start (calendar), every and start (afterDone), or offset and every (relative), read in timeZone and moved off weekend days and holidays as adjust says. The occurrences that have not opened are planned again from it; the open and finished ones stay. The same recurrence is answered unchanged, but for a relative one whose date has moved: it is planned again from the date, and stays as it was set.

rule.description: The RFC 5545 RRULE of a calendar recurrence: FREQ=YEARLY;BYMONTH=10;BYMONTHDAY=31.

start.description: A wall date or date-time: a calendar rule's start, or an afterDone recurrence's first due when nothing is done and its time of day.

every.description: An ISO 8601 duration: an afterDone recurrence's interval after the last completion, or a relative one's between anniversaries of its date.

offset.description: An ISO 8601 duration, negative before: a relative recurrence's offset from its date (-P60D).

timeZone.description: The IANA time zone it is read in; the config's, else UTC, when absent.

adjust.description: How a due date on a weekend day or a holiday moves; the config's when absent.

planned.description: The keys of the occurrences now upcoming or open, in due order.

kept.description: The keys of the open occurrences the change left as they were.

nextDueAt.description: When the earliest occurrence that is upcoming or open falls due, in epoch milliseconds; absent when none is.

unchanged.description: True when the row's recurrence was the same and dated what the row holds, so nothing was written; absent otherwise.

operations.name: complete
operations.description: Completes an occurrence: the one key names, or the earliest open one, else the earliest missed one. An open or missed occurrence is done; one that has not opened is the veto not_open, and a done or skipped one is answered unchanged. completedBy names the row that completed it, any row as references name one. An afterDone recurrence plans its next occurrence from now.

key.description: The occurrence; the earliest open, else missed, when absent.

completedBy.description: The row that completed it: its table and its key, as text.

unchanged.description: True when nothing was written; absent otherwise.

operations.name: skip
operations.description: Skips an occurrence that is upcoming, open or missed: it is finished, and the next is not held by it. A skipped or done one is answered unchanged.

operations.name: moveOne
operations.description: Moves one occurrence that is upcoming or open to another wall date-time, in the recurrence's zone, with its lead times; the rule and the other occurrences stay. A rule change drops a moved occurrence that has not opened, as it drops every one. A finished one is the veto occurrence_finished.
